column5: note
Cha explores multiple Theresa/Thérèse figures; supports name-lineage projection.
Saint Thérèse pictured performing as Joan of Arc.
Falconetti performs Joan of Arc in Dreyer's film.
Cha as authorial mediator for Yu Gwan-sun's silenced voice.
DISEUSE channels voices of silenced women including Yu Gwan-sun.
'Korean Joan of Arc' — ritual naming linking both figures.
Cha conflates Empress assassination date into 1919 frame of Yu.
Persephone myth as structural frame for exile/return.
Demeter as mother figure paralleling Huh Hyung Soon's waiting in exile.
'diseuse de bonne aventure' linked to Sibyl as prophetic/medium figure.
Bari: first mudang who journeys for healing water ↔ Diseuse as textual shaman.
'They say you spoke in tongue forbidden' — Japanese colonial rule forecloses mother's Korean.
Colonial power silences Yu Gwan-sun — imprisonment and death in Seodaemun Prison.
'Nothing has changed, we are at a standstill.' — 1980 structurally recurs 1919.
'Dear Mother, 4.19... eighteen years later' — 1960 as second iteration of colonial violence structure.
Western anatomical diagram of speech organs materializes speech as bodily labor — prefigures colonial appropriation of voice.
Eastern meridian chart vs. Western anatomy — two incommensurable knowledge systems approach the same question.
Comedy chapter (THALIA) opens with Tragedy's image — genre expectation deliberately violated.
女男 (Woman-Man) reverses conventional 男女 — father's calligraphy inscribes alternative gender grammar, countering colonial ungendering.
Divided peninsula map: 'SHE opposes Her' — geographic division as visual anchor for diasporic displacement.
Translational violence (colonial/institutional) creates the conditions for untranslatability (linguistic/semantic).
Shamanic mediation operates through cyclical time: dead time requires diseuse's invocation to become accessible.
1919 Japanese police record card photo repurposed as memorial icon — colonial documentation becomes site of mediation.
Falconetti's silent face in close-up — foreclosed speech visualized, parallel to Yu Gwan-sun's silenced voice.
'She would become, herself, demarcations.' — Diseuse internalizes colonial language's regulatory infrastructure.
식민적 언어 폭력(일본어 강제, 한국어 금지)이 허형순의 언어적 주체성을 침묵시킴. "They say you spoke in tongue forbidden" (p.45). Spillers flesh/body 구분 및 Lugones colonial-gender-system과 연동.
번역 폭력이 디쇠즈의 발화 조건 자체를 구성. 디쇠즈는 온전한 언어가 아닌 파편("noise, groan, bits torn from words")으로만 말할 수 있음. 번역 불가능성이 신체적 조건으로 내면화된 상태.
